newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans see Hitler, Einstein clones on newsstands.
newsitem.headline: Germans see Hitler, Einstein clones on newsstands.

text.p: Scientific breakthroughs on cloning stirred haunted memories in Germany of its Nazi past on Monday when a leading magazine printed a line of Adolf Hitlers marching on its cover next to Albert Einsteins and Claudia Schiffers.

Der Spiegel news magazine published a drawing showing five identical copies of the Nazi leader in his brown uniform marching next to four Einsteins, clad in baggy trousers, and three Schiffers, wearing tight-fitting mini skirts.
Standing next to the clones of Hitler, who dreamed more than half a century ago of breeding a master race, is the sheep Dolly that Scottish scientists cloned.
"Science on the way to cloning humans" reads the cover story heading, which leads a 10-page story on the subject.
"Science has entered into a frontier area that raises a host of fundamental ethical questions," the magazine wrote in its letter from the publisher.

Germans have reached with a mixture of horror and humour to the news that scientists have cloned sheep. Government ministers have assured an alarmed public humans would never be cloned and pointed out the country has stiff laws against any such attempts.

The Nazis tried to breed a "superhuman race" and performed horrific experiments on humans. Nazi scientists took part in an ignominious attempt to create an Aryan blue-eyed and blond-haired "master race".

The Nazis also adopted the "science" of eugenics, which proclaimed that some were fit to live and breed while others, such as the mentally or physically handicapped, were considered genetically inferior and had to be destroyed or sterilised.
